items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: I was with Captain Joe... he used to make that kind of money... So he didn't want to see it... I went back to New Orleans and played about six months ago... I quit and went to work in a nightclub down there.

ctx.x: It was a talk of the time. They'd come out and see what that band was playing. Well what did the band sound like? Was it like Dixieland today would you say?

Well it was a higher form because the first time wasn't usually then, had three reeds. See we had three reeds, three brass and four rhythm. Well that was a big band for those years. I was a big band. That's what I said. It was the first time to have a big band like that. And it was somewhat unusual. And we'd get to rehearsal and we'd say we were going to play this, and we had our own head arraignment and Mason because we met, what we were going to play, he'd write out, we'd get together and we were going to play…
then go into something else. I can't think of any of that number. It's one of New Orleans'
